best_for: People replaying old DOS games on a modern PC or Mac who want them to look and sound right without hand-tuning shaders and MIDI setups.

points.title: Your DOSBox configs still work
points.text: DOSBox Staging continues the original DOSBox, and existing configuration files keep working. It also supports portable and layered configuration files.

points.title: CRT look with no setup
points.text: A built-in CRT emulation adapts to your screen from 720p up to 4K, so games look closer to how they did on a tube monitor. Custom shaders are supported too.

points.title: Period sound built in
points.text: Roland MT-32 and SC-55 emulation and a FluidSynth MIDI synth are included, so games with music for those devices play it without extra software.

points.title: Graphics and network
points.text: It emulates VGA, EGA, CGA, Hercules and the 3dfx Voodoo 1 card. Ethernet, modem and IPX options cover old multiplayer games.

points.title: 64-bit only now
points.text: Version 0.83.1 needs 64-bit Windows 8, 10 or 11 on x64; there is no Arm build for Windows. The Mac .dmg is universal and needs macOS 12 or later. A dedicated graphics card is recommended on laptops.

points.title: Linux: Flatpak or tarball
points.text: The Flatpak here is verified on Flathub, so it comes from the DOSBox Staging team. The project's own Linux download is an x86_64 tarball, and it supports only its official builds, not distro packages.

points.title: Free and open
points.text: No account, no price, GPL-2.0 or later. The Windows installer here can install for one user or all users, and the Windows listing keeps 9 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
